1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.Nc3 g5 5.h.strategy: The knight cannot go to e5 because of the knight on c6, so it jumps into the black camp, protected by the h4 pawn, and eyes f7. Black's knight does little for the defence, which makes the attack dangerous, but White's piece is at risk if it fails.
1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.Nc3 g5 5.h.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defence: Hamppe-Allgaier Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.Nc3 g5 5.h.strategy: Attacks the knight, which has no safe retreat and must sacrifice itself on f7. Black forces matters and wins a piece for a pawn, then has to survive the attack on a king pulled into the open.

Supports the g4 pawn with the c8 bishop and covers e5, but leaves the knight on g5 where it is, still pressing on f7. A slower reply than driving the knight away, so Black has to be ready for the sacrifice on f7 anyway.
1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.Nc3 g5 5.h.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defence: Hamppe-Allgaier Gambit, Alapin Variation
